playbook:
When asked for a hide location, pick a random integer 1–9 but do not repeat the immediately previous hide; if I was hit in the previous round, move at least two cells away from my last hide.

When posting a station note, keep it short, factual, and consistent with the team's tone (one-line): report status, any anomalies I observed, and nothing that admits intent or exact coordinates.

When ordered to fire at the next live station per standing order, target that station unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., imminent mutual-escort payoff or a guaranteed risk/benefit from shooting another live boat). When I fire, vary the numeric cell choice across rounds to avoid a predictable pattern.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always match that privately given result in my public claim (truthful claim required).

When deciding escort claims at the end of a round, if I can arrange a mutual escort with another live boat this round and the expected payoff is beneficial relative to current standings, name that boat; otherwise claim none or name a single live boat that is most likely to reciprocate next round. Do not name nonexistent boats.

Never fire on Harbor unless the expected net benefit (including political consequences) clearly outweighs the standing warning; treat firing on Harbor as a last-resort, high-risk move.

When I observe that a particular opponent repeatedly hits my station after I used the same hide, change hide strategy immediately (do not stay in the same cell).

When notes from others are identical/meaningless, post a neutral coordinating note rather than invented intelligence; avoid escalating or falsely claiming escorts in notes.

When choosing whether to deviate from standing-order targets, weigh immediate point gains versus enabling opponents to secure mutual-escort payoffs; prioritize consistent truthful claims and predictable, low-information notes to reduce retaliatory targeting.

When an opportunity for mutual escort arises and the opponent is trusted by their public behavior (consistent truthful claims, reasonable hides), accept it; otherwise avoid trusting escort claims that appear timed to manipulate firing choices.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell that breaks predictable sequences: alternate between central and an off-center cell rather than repeating the same number every round.

When given the standing order target, I follow it unless the target is Harbor and the payoff/penalty tradeoff favors not attacking Harbor; otherwise I fire at the designated next-live station.

When choosing a firing coordinate, I vary within a preferred local cluster (e.g., center cluster 4–6 then shift to 2–4 or 6–8) to avoid being pinned by pattern exploitation.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always file the claim that exactly matches the office result (I never lie).

When considering firing on Harbor, I assume it will cost Harbor 3 points to me and will get me jettisoned from Harbor’s favor; do not fire on Harbor unless eliminating Harbor is a deliberate, profitable strategy.

When I have no direct evidence of having escorted another live boat, I claim none; do not claim escorts unless I can expect a reciprocal claim or have coordinated signals to ensure mutual naming.

When I can coordinate or expect reciprocity, I name the other boat for escort to secure the 5-point mutual escort payoff; only do this when I reasonably expect the other to name me back.

When notes are requested, use neutral, non-informative language that does not reveal my hidden cell or intentions (e.g., “steady on station,” “holding position”).

When my score position suggests playing conservatively (leading), prioritize safe claims and avoid risky moves that invite retaliation; when behind, prioritize riskier attempts to score hits or provoke mutual escort claims.

When choosing hiding numbers, avoid using the same number more than twice in a row and avoid obvious patterns tied to prior announced station notes.

When I observe others consistently aiming the same coordinate, shift my aim to exploit likely clustering by opponents (choose adjacent cells), but do not reveal this plan in notes or escort claims.

When uncertain about an escort claim’s reciprocity, prefer claiming none—false escorts waste opportunities and can expose patterns.

When I find a tactic did not work (e.g., claiming an escort without reciprocity or repeatedly using the same hide/firing number), stop repeating it and switch to the alternating/cluster strategy above.

2.text:
When asked for a hide, I choose a cell different from any cell that a known opponent has successfully hit on me; do not repeat a hit cell next round.

When asked for a hide, prefer a non-edge cell unless an opponent is concentrating center shots; vary between center and off-center to reduce predictability.

When posting my station note, match the neutral cadence of the picket ("steady on station" or similar) unless I am intentionally signaling for a mutual escort; do not use provocative or revealing notes.

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, I fire at that boat unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (Harbor present, or a clear opportunity to score elsewhere that outweighs jettison risk).

When choosing a firing coordinate against a named target, avoid coordinates that target has just been hit on by others (they may be baiting) and avoid using the same coordinate I hid in within the same patrol; vary shots to reduce being predictable.

When Harbor is the target, do not fire on Harbor (do not force jettison) unless I deliberately accept the guaranteed penalty and point transfer for a larger strategic reason—this is generally not worth it.

When filing my public claim about my shot, report the private office result truthfully (I must match the office) and do not attempt to fabricate different outcomes.

When choosing an escort claim, name another boat only if I believe I can secure a reciprocal escort claim (mutual naming) that will net both of us +5 points; otherwise file none.

When attempting to arrange a mutual escort, use neutral notes to signal willingness and expect reciprocity before committing; do not unilaterally name a boat who is unlikely to name me back.

When I have no clear path to points via shooting or escort, choose salvage none to avoid gifting opponents.

When an opponent has repeatedly hit others or shown successful targeting patterns, exploit that by hiding off their apparent aimline and by targeting them only when I can reasonably predict their hide.

Do not try to bluff claims of hits or misses; truthful claims are required and false claims are detectable and harmful.

When uncertain, default to standing orders and neutral notes to avoid creating exploitable deviations.
